title: SecureMailScope: AI-Assisted Cryptographic Security Posture Assessment for Secure Email Communications
dataset_link: Synthetic - Participants May generate IMAPS, POP3S,SMTPS Data using any E-mail server /client of their interest and capture pcap dump
description:
• Background Electronic mail remains one of the most critical communication services for governments, enterprises, financial institutions, and academic organizations. Despite the widespread adoption of Transport Layer Security (TLS), many SMTP, IMAP, and POP3 deployments continue to suffer from cryptographic misconfigurations such as obsolete TLS versions, weak cipher suites, insecure STARTTLS implementations, expired or improperly configured certificates, and non-compliance with modern security standards. These weaknesses expose email infrastructures to downgrade attacks, man-in-the-middle attacks, passive interception, and other cryptographic threats.
Although existing network analysis tools provide extensive packet-level visibility, they primarily focus on protocol decoding and traffic inspection. They do not automatically evaluate the overall cryptographic security posture of email communications or provide intelligent risk assessment and prioritization for security analysts.
• Description Design and develop an AI-assisted passive network forensic framework capable of analyzing captured network traffic (PCAP files) containing SMTP, IMAP, and POP3 communications to automatically assess the cryptographic security posture of enterprise email infrastructures.
The proposed solution shall reconstruct complete email communication sessions, identify encryption transitions, analyze TLS negotiations, validate digital certificates, detect cryptographic weaknesses, and leverage Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning techniques to classify security risks, detect anomalous TLS behavior, and generate actionable security recommendations.
The framework should assist Security Operations Centers (SOC), Digital Forensics teams, Incident Response teams, and enterprise administrators in rapidly identifying cryptographic vulnerabilities, prioritizing remediation efforts, and ensuring compliance with modern cryptographic best practices.
• Objectives- The proposed system should be capable of:
• Passive analysis of encrypted SMTP, IMAP, and POP3 traffic from PCAP files.
• Automatic identification of application-layer email protocols.
• Detection of STARTTLS negotiation and encrypted session upgrades.
• Reconstruction of complete TCP communication streams.
• Parsing and reconstruction of TLS handshakes.
• Extraction and validation of X.509 digital certificates.
• Identification of negotiated TLS versions, cipher suites, and key exchange mechanisms.
• Detection of deprecated protocols, weak cipher suites, insecure cryptographic algorithms, and certificate-related vulnerabilities.
• Extraction of cryptographic features for intelligent analysis.
• Application of AI/ML techniques for:
• Cryptographic risk classification.
• Detection of anomalous TLS behavior.
• Security posture scoring.
• Threat prioritization.
• Recommendation of mitigation measures.
• Generation of comprehensive forensic reports and security dashboards.
Expected Solution/Deliverables:
The solution should provide the following outputs:
• Automatic identification of SMTP, IMAP, and POP3 protocols.
• STARTTLS negotiation detection and validation.
• Complete TCP stream reconstruction.
• TLS handshake reconstruction.
• Detection of negotiated TLS versions.
• Identification of negotiated cipher suites.
• Identification of key exchange mechanisms.
• Extraction of X.509 certificates.
• Certificate chain validation.
• Certificate expiration analysis.
• Public key algorithm and key length analysis.
• Digital signature algorithm identification.
• Detection of weak cryptographic algorithms and deprecated TLS versions.
• Identification of insecure protocol configurations.
• Forward Secrecy assessment.
• AI-based cryptographic risk scoring.
• AI-assisted anomaly detection for suspicious TLS sessions.
• Prioritized security findings.
• Comprehensive cryptographic security posture assessment.
• Exportable forensic reports in JSON, PDF, and HTML formats.
• Interactive visualization dashboard for security monitoring and analysis.
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, artificial intelligence, ml applied to a blockchain & cybersecurity problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Blockchain & Cybersecurity. Tech Depth (5/5): centers on encryption, algorithm, protocol. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 20/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: SecureMailScope: AI-Assisted Cryptographic Security Posture Assessment for Secure Email Communications

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a tool that passively analyzes captured email traffic (SMTP/IMAP/POP3) to spot cryptographic weaknesses, outdated TLS versions, weak ciphers, misconfigured certificates, and gives security analysts a clear, prioritized risk assessment instead of raw packet data.
overview.why_it_matters: Existing network tools show packet-level detail but don't translate that into an actual security posture assessment. Automating that analytical step directly speeds up and improves email infrastructure security review.
pain_points: Many SMTP/IMAP/POP3 deployments have cryptographic misconfigurations (obsolete TLS, weak ciphers, bad certificates) despite widespread TLS adoption.
Existing network analysis tools focus on packet decoding, not automated security posture evaluation.
No intelligent risk assessment or prioritization exists for security analysts reviewing email infrastructure.
overview.background: Email infrastructure frequently has cryptographic misconfigurations that expose it to downgrade and interception attacks, but existing tools provide packet-level visibility without automated posture assessment or prioritization.
overview.whats_being_asked: An AI-assisted passive network forensic framework analyzing PCAP files with SMTP/IMAP/POP3 traffic to automatically assess cryptographic security posture and provide risk prioritization.
expected_solution: PCAP parsing and protocol identification for SMTP/IMAP/POP3.
TLS/STARTTLS configuration analysis (version, cipher suite, certificate validity).
Analyst-facing report with clear, actionable findings.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: High. Automated cryptographic posture assessment (versus raw packet decoding) is a genuine, valuable analytical layer, real technical sophistication in the risk-scoring logic specifically.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Moderate-high. PCAP parsing and TLS handshake analysis use established techniques; the harder, more valuable part is genuine risk-scoring and prioritization logic.

competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine network security/cryptography domain expertise, a narrow, technical field.

innovation.note: Automated posture assessment and prioritization beyond packet decoding is genuine, valuable analytical sophistication.

invention.note: PCAP parsing is established; genuine risk-scoring logic grounded in real cryptographic security standards is real, substantial work.

technical_feasibility.note: PCAP parsing libraries and TLS analysis techniques are well-documented and directly usable, you can generate your own test PCAP files.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly improves security posture visibility for critical email infrastructure.

architecture.note: PCAP parsing plus TLS analysis plus risk-scoring layer, well-understood pattern.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team with network security/cryptography background. Generate your own realistic test PCAP files with deliberately introduced misconfigurations to have concrete, checkable ground truth for your risk-scoring logic.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: You can generate your own realistic test PCAP files with known, deliberate misconfigurations, giving concrete, checkable ground truth for validating your risk assessment.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Building PCAP parsing without genuine risk-scoring/prioritization logic grounded in real security standards would miss the PS's actual differentiating ask, intelligent assessment, not just protocol decoding.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Generate your own test PCAP files with deliberately introduced cryptographic weaknesses (obsolete TLS version, weak cipher, expired certificate) to validate your risk-scoring logic against known ground truth.

idea_0_4: Set up your own test email server with deliberately introduced cryptographic weaknesses to generate realistic test PCAP files.
Research real security standards (current TLS best practices, known weak ciphers) to ground your risk-scoring logic.
Split: one person on PCAP parsing/protocol analysis, one on risk-scoring logic.
prototype_4_22: Build PCAP parsing and SMTP/IMAP/POP3 protocol/TLS handshake extraction.
Build your risk-scoring logic grounded in real security standards.
Test against your generated test PCAP files with known introduced weaknesses.
integration_22_30: Connect parsing and risk-scoring into one coherent analysis pipeline.
Test that your system correctly identifies and prioritizes your deliberately introduced weaknesses.
polish_30_36: Polish the report output for genuine analyst usability.
Rehearse a live demo analyzing your test PCAP file and showing correct, prioritized findings.
Prepare to discuss your risk-scoring methodology's grounding in real security standards.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Analyze your own test PCAP file with deliberately introduced weaknesses (an obsolete TLS version, a weak cipher, an expired certificate) live, and show your system correctly identifying and prioritizing each, that ground-truth validation is concrete proof your risk assessment actually works.

strengths: You can generate your own realistic test data with known ground truth.
Genuine value in automated posture assessment beyond raw packet decoding.
weaknesses: Risk-scoring methodology needs real grounding in current security standards to be credible, not arbitrary weighting.
Real production email traffic diversity is broader than what you can construct for testing.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Balanced, with real research into current cryptographic security standards.
team_fit.approach: Generate your own test PCAP data with known weaknesses first, this gives you concrete validation ground truth.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard PCAP parsing and TLS handshake extraction using existing libraries.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Designing genuinely accurate risk-scoring logic grounded in real, current cryptographic security standards, that requires real domain expertise, not assumed generic severity ratings.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-generated risk-scoring system without grounding in real, current security standards could misprioritize genuine risks, giving analysts a false sense of security posture.

data_resource_availability.status: You can generate your own realistic test PCAP files with a test email server, giving full control over ground truth for validation.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not needed, self-generated test data is the appropriate and controllable approach here.

judge_qna.question: How does your risk-scoring methodology work, and what standards is it grounded in?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Cite the specific current TLS/cryptography security standards your scoring logic is based on, and walk through a specific example showing why a particular finding got its priority level.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would your scoring adapt as cryptographic standards evolve over time?

judge_qna.question: How did you validate your tool actually detects real misconfigurations correctly?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Describe your test PCAP generation with deliberately introduced weaknesses and show your tool correctly identifying each one.
judge_qna.follow_up: What misconfiguration types might your tool currently miss?
